overview: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM) is a flagship initiative by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, aimed at developing 300 Rurban clusters across the country by provisioning economic, social, and physical infrastructure facilities. It seeks to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services, and create well-planned Rurban clusters through convergence of various government schemes and Critical Gap Funding (CGF). The mission focuses on geographically contiguous villages with populations ranging from 5,000 to 50,000, depending on terrain, and aims to bridge the rural-urban divide while preserving rural community life with urban-like amenities.
objectives: Stimulate local economic development with emphasis on reduction of poverty and unemployment in rural areas
Enhance basic services and create well planned Rurban clusters
Bridge the rural-urban divide in economic, technological, and service-related aspects
Spread development in the region and attract investment in rural areas
Develop 300 Rurban clusters over the next five years across all States and UTs
Strengthen rural areas by provisioning economic, social, and infrastructure amenities for sustainable and balanced regional development
Ensure organized development of clusters through delineation as planning areas under relevant State Planning Acts
Promote convergence of Central, Centrally Sponsored, and State Government schemes for fund mobilization
eligibility: The mission targets geographically contiguous villages forming clusters with a population of about 25,000 to 50,000 in plain and coastal areas, and 5,000 to 15,000 in desert, hilly, or tribal areas. Clusters must follow administrative convergence units of Gram Panchayats and be within a single block/tehsil. Selection is based on parameters such as decadal growth in rural population, non-farm work force participation, presence of economic clusters, tourism and pilgrimage significance, and proximity to transport corridors, with separate approaches for Tribal and Non-Tribal districts.
benefits: Benefits include provision of economic activities, skill development and local entrepreneurship training, infrastructure amenities such as piped water supply, sanitation, solid and liquid waste management, village streets and drains, street lights, inter-village road connectivity, public transport, LPG connections, digital literacy, Citizen Service Centres (CSCs), agro-processing, agri-services, storage and warehousing, fully equipped mobile health units, upgradation of school/higher education facilities, and digital literacy. Financial support is provided through Critical Gap Funding (CGF) to supplement convergence of scheme funds.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Critical Gap Funding (CGF) under SPMRM, which supplements the shortfall in funding available through convergence of various Central Sector, Centrally Sponsored, and State Government schemes. For plain and coastal areas, CGF is up to 30% of the project cost or Rs. 30 crores per cluster, whichever is lesser. For desert, hilly, and tribal areas, CGF is up to 30% of the project cost or Rs. 15 crores per cluster, whichever is lesser. Funds are released in three instalments: 30%, 30%, and 40% of the total CGF approved, with the SNA transferring 35% of the CGF received as third instalment to the project and the balance 5% after completion of all project components.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 30 crores per cluster for plain areas and Rs. 15 crores per cluster for desert, hilly, and tribal areas, or 30% of project cost, whichever is lesser
application_process: 1. Identification of potential Rurban clusters by the Ministry and States based on demographic, economic, tourism, and transportation criteria. 2. Selection of clusters by State Governments within identified sub-districts, considering performance parameters like decadal rural population growth, rise in land values, non-farm work participation, girls' enrollment in secondary schools, bank account penetration under PMJDY, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) performance, and good governance initiatives. 3. Preparation of Integrated Cluster Action Plan (ICAP) by State Nodal Agency (SNA) with support from State Technical Support Agencies (STSAs), covering baseline studies, required interventions, resource convergence, and CGF estimation. 4. Submission of ICAP to the Ministry for approval by the Empowered Committee. 5. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) for approved components. 6. Approval of DPR by State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC). 7. Release of funds in instalments as per financial concurrence. 8. Implementation of project components through convergence of schemes and CGF. 9. Operations and maintenance for ten years post-implementation. 10. Monitoring and evaluation through quarterly reports, utilization certificates, and site visits.
required_documents: Progress report of work on ground
Setting up of State Project Management Unit (SPMU)
Setting up of District Project Management Unit (DPMU)
Setting up of Cluster Development and Management Unit (CDMU)
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per the five-yearly iteration of ICAPs and fund release proposals.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
contact_details: Email: mis[dot]rurban[at]nic[dot]in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence
caveats: CGF is limited to 30% of project cost or Rs. 30 crores per cluster (plain areas) and Rs. 15 crores per cluster (desert/hilly/tribal areas), whichever is lesser
Fund release is contingent upon utilization of 60% or more funds available in the State Nodal Account
State must release corresponding State Share against previous central releases
Expenditure projection for next 6 months must be submitted with fund release proposal
State Project Management Unit (SPMU) must be set up with adequate professionals as per Framework of Implementation
Third instalment of CGF (35%) is released only after approval of DPR by SLEC and 60% CGF utilization
Final 5% of CGF is released only after submission of Audited Statement of expenditure, completion of Planning Notification, publication of Spatial Plan, and setup of SPMU, DPMU, and CDMU
States must ensure Geo-tagging initiation and work verification for at least 5% of works executed
All funds must be transferred to State Nodal Account within 15 days of receiving central share in State treasury
